findings.desc: CHK-002 adversarial:0 was authored from a false premise and one of its two clauses is unsatisfiable on this branch. The intent text reads 'the local d3 hard-failure branch in scripts/build-web.mjs survives the port AND dossier.js is concatenated after app.js, not before'. The d3 hard-failure change exists only as an uncommitted edit in the MAIN checkout; it is not committed on story/B-9f2c and it is not upstream either. Verified two ways: grep -c 'd3 is missing' packages/graph/scripts/build-web.mjs returns 0 on this branch, and the CHK-002 implementer independently reported build-web.mjs is now byte-identical to upstream. So no work on this branch can either satisfy or violate that clause. The load-order clause is the real risk and IS proven: build-web.mjs concatenates app.js at line 33, playback.js at 36 and dossier.js at 40, and the recorded evidence for this intent pins that ordering with a negative control. No evidence was fabricated for the d3 clause; the implementer recorded its voiding in the evidence note. Deliberately NOT fixed by rewriting the intent: verificationIntent is frozen after PLAN by design, and checklist_update correctly refused the edit. Rewriting a frozen intent mid-DEV to match what was actually built is exactly the self-absolution the freeze exists to prevent. Filing this instead so the mismatch is auditable rather than silently reworded.
findings.resolvedReason: Accepted as a documented, non-blocking record rather than fixed, because the only available fix is prohibited by design. The defect is in the WORDING of a frozen PLAN artifact, not in shipped behavior: CHK-002:adversarial:0 bundles two clauses, and the d3 hard-failure clause is unsatisfiable on this branch. Independently re-verified three ways by the test-coverage reviewer (B-9f2c:RP-004), which confirmed the d3 branch exists only as an uncommitted diff in the unrelated main checkout, is absent from git log and grep on story/B-9f2c, and is absent from upstream proof-or-stop-graph as well. The load-order clause, which is the real risk that intent exists to guard, IS genuinely evidenced: RP-004 reconstructed the regression itself, moving dossier.js ahead of app.js in build-web.mjs, and confirmed the probe fails closed with DOSSIER_LOAD_ORDER_FAIL exit 1. No evidence was fabricated for the void clause. Rewriting the intent to match what was built was attempted and correctly REFUSED by checklist_update, since verificationIntent is frozen after PLAN; doing so would be exactly the self-absolution that freeze exists to prevent. Per CLAUDE.md defect triage, this is non-blocking (low severity, no gate distortion, no acceptance impact: AB-001 does not bind CHK-002:adversarial:0) and unclaimed by any checklist item, so it is recorded and deferred with full evidence rather than fixed by scope creep. RP-004 explicitly reviewed this handling and agreed with it. Follow-up for a future story, if desired: split multi-clause verificationIntent entries into one clause each at authoring time, so a single void clause cannot strand an otherwise-satisfied intent.

findings.desc: doc-code-drift: docs/requirements/decisions/graph-command-migration.md:111-115 (section 'Test-surface placement') states 'Two test lists in this repository are separately maintained, and neither is a subset of the other: validate.commands in the project config, and test:serial-reference in the root package.json.' This is incomplete: packages/main/src/tasks/full-suite-runner.ts's RESOURCE_POLICY (lines 116-159) is a THIRD fail-closed membership authority -- entriesFromSerialReference (full-suite-runner.ts:216-227) throws 'canonical inventory mismatch unknownPolicy=[...]' and aborts the whole suite (called at line 590 of main(), before any test entry is scheduled) if a test:serial-reference member has no RESOURCE_POLICY entry. This story's own CHK-005 checklist context explicitly modeled its plan on this doc's 'TWO separate test-surface lists' framing and, as a direct consequence, registered the new graph-story-flag-smoke task in validate.commands and test:serial-reference but not in RESOURCE_POLICY -- causing npm test to abort in 858ms with exactly the unknownPolicy error the code comments describe, which blocked done_required_validate and forced a TEST->DEV->REVIEW bounce (fixed in commit f4e9acdd21). The code's own comments at full-suite-runner.ts:145-146 and :151-153 record that this identical trap was already hit twice before by other stories (B-49ed, B-cdf6), meaning the canonical decision doc has been silently incomplete across at least three incidents. A future implementer who reads only this doc (as CHK-005 did) will reproduce the same suite-aborting failure. Severity high: this is the specific reproducible-bug-inducing doc gap the review task explicitly asked to check for, and the doc is the canonical decision reference cited by this story's own checklist relatedDocs.
findings.resolvedReason: Fixed in commit 527de168c1. The 'Test-surface placement' section of docs/requirements/decisions/graph-command-migration.md now says THREE membership authorities instead of Two, and enumerates them: validate.commands in the project config, test:serial-reference in the root package.json plus the test:<name> script it names, and RESOURCE_POLICY in packages/main/src/tasks/full-suite-runner.ts. The rewrite explains why the third is the most punishing to omit, quoting the actual fail-closed behavior: entriesFromSerialReference throws 'canonical inventory mismatch unknownPolicy=[...]' and aborts the ENTIRE root suite rather than skipping the member, so forgetting it takes down npm test for the whole repository rather than under-testing one task. It also records that this has now bitten three stories (B-cdf6, B-49ed, and this one) and states plainly that registering a new test task means editing all three lists. Every claim in the new text was verified against code before committing: all three registration sites confirmed present for test:graph-story-flag-smoke, and the throw string confirmed verbatim at full-suite-runner.ts:224. Per the global working preference that a corrected fact must be fanned out rather than fixed in one place, the rest of the documentation was swept for the same stale framing: CLAUDE.md does not make this claim, and of the other decision docs mentioning test:serial-reference (done-full-test-gate-execution-plan.md, test-runner-consolidation-plan.md, proof-or-stop-identity-migration.md) none asserts a two-list model, so graph-command-migration.md was the only stale source. The reviewer's diagnosis was exactly right and is worth restating: this doc is cited in CHK-005's relatedDocs and CHK-005 copied its two-list framing, so the document intended to prevent this trap was itself the proximate cause of the third occurrence.

findings.desc: packages/main/src/tasks/graph-story-flag-smoke.ts CHK-005:adversarial:0 pinned command only re-verifies lattice.config.json validate.commands and package.json (test:<name> script + test:serial-reference membership) -- it never reads packages/main/src/tasks/full-suite-runner.ts's RESOURCE_POLICY, the THIRD fail-closed membership authority that was the actual root cause of the done_required_validate failure this round (npm test aborted in 858ms with 'canonical inventory mismatch unknownPolicy=[test:graph-story-flag-smoke]', fixed in f4e9acdd21). Negative control on a scratch copy (git show HEAD:packages/main/src/tasks/full-suite-runner.ts with the RESOURCE_POLICY repoRead('test:graph-story-flag-smoke') line at line 159 removed, never touching the tracked file) confirms the pinned adversarial command still prints SELECTOR_BOTH_SURFACES_REGISTERED and exits 0 against the real repo's lattice.config.json/package.json, i.e. it is a false positive for exactly the class of regression it claims to guard against ('the task is registered in BOTH surfaces, so membership in one list is never mistaken for coverage by the other'). The CHK-005 verificationIntent wording is frozen after PLAN so it cannot be reworded now (same disposition as F-001); this finding records the gap so the pinned probe (or a follow-up story) can add a third assertion reading RESOURCE_POLICY membership, matching the corrected 'three membership authorities' text just landed in docs/requirements/decisions/graph-command-migration.md by F-002. Not blocking: the live defect is already fixed (f4e9acdd21) and independently confirmed by the commit chain through done_required_validate; this is a test-completeness gap in the regression guard, not a currently-failing check.
findings.resolvedReason: Confirmed real, and accepted as a documented residual rather than fixed, because every available fix is refused by design. INDEPENDENTLY REPRODUCED: on scratch copies (tracked files untouched) the pinned adversarial probe for CHK-005:adversarial:0 reads only lattice.config.json and package.json, so it prints SELECTOR_BOTH_SURFACES_REGISTERED and exits 0 even when the RESOURCE_POLICY entry in full-suite-runner.ts is absent -- a false positive for exactly the regression class the intent names. The reviewer reached the same result by the same method. TWO FIXES WERE ATTEMPTED AND BOTH CORRECTLY REFUSED. First, rewording the frozen verificationIntent: refused, verificationIntent is frozen after PLAN and checklist_update rejects the edit; rewriting an intent mid-flight to match what was built is the self-absolution the freeze exists to prevent. Second, attaching a strictly better probe as supplementary evidence on the same intentRef: refused with [receipt_command_mismatch] 'the verification pin is immutable'. That refusal is correct on the merits -- if a caller could swap an intent's pinned command after the fact, the pin would prove nothing, since anyone could retroactively redefine what an intent verifies. The better probe was nonetheless written and validated: it additionally requires the RESOURCE_POLICY entry, and a negative control on a scratch copy with only that line stripped makes it exit 1 with 'FAIL validate=true scripts=true serialReference=true resourcePolicy=false' while the original probe still exits 0 on the same input. WHY THE RESIDUAL RISK IS LOW: the underlying registration is present and correct in all three authorities, verified by the concept lane invoking entriesFromSerialReference directly and observing unknownPolicy=[]; the real defense against this regression class is not this probe but the root suite itself, which fails closed at module load, and npm test is a DONE-required command, so deleting the RESOURCE_POLICY entry would abort the suite and block DONE regardless of what this probe reports. Per CLAUDE.md defect triage this is medium severity, advisory in round 2, claimed by no checklist item beyond the frozen intent, and distorts no gate that is not already independently enforced, so it is recorded and deferred with full evidence rather than closed by scope creep. FOLLOW-UP FOR A DEDICATED STORY: author multi-authority membership intents as one intent per authority, so a single probe can never claim coverage of a surface it does not read; and consider making the phrase 'BOTH surfaces' in any future intent a lint-able smell now that three authorities exist. The doc that caused the original two-surface framing was corrected under F-002 in commit 527de168c1, which removes the upstream cause for future stories.

findings.desc: doc-code-drift: docs/requirements/decisions/graph-command-migration.md:196-200 still says 'the six tasks run through TWO separately-maintained mechanisms, the same split the "Test-surface placement" section above describes' -- but the F-002 fix (commit 527de168c1) rewrote that section to describe THREE membership authorities (validate.commands, test:serial-reference, RESOURCE_POLICY), not two. This paragraph was not updated in the same fix, so the doc now cross-references its own earlier section with a framing that section no longer has, and the claim is also inaccurate on its own terms: test:process-fact-contract (one of the six tasks this paragraph is about) IS registered in RESOURCE_POLICY (packages/main/src/tasks/full-suite-runner.ts:180), so it participates in all three authorities, not 'only through test:serial-reference' as implied by the two-mechanism framing. This is exactly the kind of stale cross-reference the CLAUDE.md global preference on fanning out corrections warns about: fixing one occurrence of a wrong fact while leaving a second occurrence in the same file. Severity medium: this is process-fact documentation drift within a decisions doc that CHK-005's relatedDocs cites as the trap-prevention source, so a future story reading only this later paragraph could re-inherit the same two-authority misunderstanding that already caused three prior incidents (B-cdf6, B-49ed, B-9f2c CHK-005).
findings.resolvedReason: Fixed in commit 9a05f7677e. The reviewer was right on both counts, and both were verified against code before the edit. First, the stale cross-reference: the paragraph said the six process-fact tasks run through 'two separately-maintained mechanisms, the same split the Test-surface placement section above describes', but the F-002 fix had already rewritten that section to describe THREE authorities, so the sentence pointed at a description that no longer existed. Second, the independent factual error: it claimed test:process-fact-contract is 'reached only through the root test:serial-reference list', yet that task carries repoRead('test:process-fact-contract') at full-suite-runner.ts:180, so it participates in all three authorities. The paragraph now says three separately-maintained membership authorities, names the RESOURCE_POLICY entry explicitly, and adds the consequence that a test:serial-reference member missing its RESOURCE_POLICY entry aborts the whole root suite rather than being skipped. This finding is a direct hit on the global working preference about fanning corrections out: my F-002 fix corrected one occurrence and missed a second occurrence IN THE SAME FILE, which is exactly the failure mode that preference exists to prevent. Corrected the process this time rather than just the text: after the edit I swept the whole file (grep for 'two separately|two test lists|two mechanisms|two membership' returns nothing) and then the entire live docs corpus including CLAUDE.md, README.md and AGENTS.md; the only two remaining hits are unrelated (docs/evidence-integrity-program-spec.md is about evidence-integrity mechanisms, and milestone-status-done-gate-reconciliation.md's 'both surfaces' refers to two callers of a shared predicate). Frozen story artifacts under docs/story/actives were deliberately excluded as historical record rather than living docs.

findings.desc: Recorded on behalf of the test-coverage reviewer, which identified this but could not register it because the review-inventory epoch RIE-004 was already FINALIZED and consumed. Commit dcf54ecff3 adapted verify-missing-assets-fail.mjs to main's new on-demand client build, but its recovery branch was a genuine coverage weakening rather than a pure contract adaptation: the success condition reduced to fs.existsSync(assets/app.html) plus an OR-style output substring match on 'building browser client' or 'graph serving'. It never checked d3.min.js, never checked the served content, and never bound the log line to who produced it. The reviewer proved this with a negative control on a scratchpad copy: feeding the branch's exact logic a fabricated output containing only 'graph serving' with rebuilt=true produced ZERO failures, so a handler writing any bytes to app.html (truncated, stale or corrupt) and logging the right words would pass a check whose entire documented purpose is proving a missing or broken browser client is never silently served. Severity is medium rather than high because production code independently re-checks both app.html and d3.min.js in ensureGraphClientBuilt and throws before any serving line prints, so the gap is not exploitable in isolation; but it would go silent the moment that handler-side check regressed. FIXED rather than deferred, in commit 4912d8390a: the recovery branch now also requires the rebuilt app.html to parse as HTML, to contain openStoryDossier (the inlined shell a real build produces), to not be implausibly small, and to be accompanied by the required d3.min.js bundle. Verified by re-running the reviewer's own scenario: a 42-byte stub with a 'graph serving' line is now CAUGHT on two independent grounds where it previously produced no failures, and npm --prefix packages/graph run check still exits 0.
findings.resolvedReason: Fixed in commit 4912d8390a, and the fix itself was then reviewed and repaired again in 22eb158523 (F-006). The weakening the test-coverage lane proved: the recovery branch accepted fs.existsSync(app.html) plus an OR-style output substring, so a handler writing any bytes to app.html and logging the right words would pass a check whose documented purpose is proving a broken client is never silently served; the reviewer's negative control produced zero failures for a corrupt stub. The recovery branch now additionally requires the rebuilt page to parse as an HTML document, to contain openStoryDossier (the registration line dossier.js:1118 emits and build-web.mjs inlines, so a meaningful marker rather than an incidental string), to exceed a 100000-byte floor (the four concatenated shell sources total 498019 bytes, so roughly 3.4x headroom, verified by the quality lane), and to be accompanied by the d3.min.js bundle that ensureGraphClientBuilt also treats as required output. Verified by re-running the reviewer's own scenario: a 42-byte stub carrying a 'graph serving' line is now caught on two independent grounds where it previously produced no failures. A residual limit remains and is recorded separately as F-007 (a deliberately padded stub containing the marker can still satisfy all four checks; closing that fully needs a digest derived from build inputs rather than fixed markers), deferred as low severity per CLAUDE.md triage since production independently re-checks both files.

findings.desc: packages/graph/scripts/verify-missing-assets-fail.mjs:53-89 (current HEAD, unchanged since 4912d8390a): `rebuilt = fs.existsSync(asset)` (line 53) is sampled once, right after execFileSync's 60s timeout fires, and races the child's own spawnSync(npm run build) inside ensureGraphClientBuilt. Reproduced live in this worktree with the unmodified script: `npm --prefix packages/graph run check` failed at verify-missing-assets-fail with MISSING_ASSET_HANDLING_BROKEN, even though assets/app.html and assets/d3.min.js were both freshly rebuilt (mtimes matched the run within the same second) -- the rebuild genuinely succeeded, just moments after the 60s sample point. Because the script falls into the else (recovery-impossible) branch whenever `rebuilt` samples false, and the SIGKILL cleanup at the bottom only runs `if (rebuilt) { ...kill... } else if (held.length) { ...report... }`, the still-serving graph process was left running and leaked, listening on the port (verified via lsof/ps: PID 45353 for GRAPH_VERIFY_PORT=8819, uncleaned by the script, had to be killed manually). Two concrete effects: (1) the commit's own stated goal -- 'the command must never end up listening while the client is still missing' -- is inverted in this exact scenario: the client WAS built (so nothing is missing), yet the check reports MISSING_ASSET_HANDLING_BROKEN and simultaneously fails to kill or even report the real leaked listener, because that report path is also gated on `!rebuilt`. (2) repeated runs of `npm run check` on a loaded machine will accumulate leaked `node bin/proof-or-stop.js graph --port=8819` processes with no diagnostic pointing at the actual cause (a timing race, not a broken recovery path). This is a genuine, reproduced-twice defect distinct from the assertion-strength gap already fixed in 4912d8390a (content validation of the rebuilt app.html/d3.min.js) -- that fix hardens the `rebuilt===true` branch's assertions but does not touch how `rebuilt` itself is determined, so the race is unaffected by it.
findings.resolvedReason: Fixed in commit 22eb158523. The quality lane reproduced both halves live and was right on both. RACE: `rebuilt` was sampled once immediately after execFileSync's 60s timeout, which can fire while the child is still inside its own npm run build, so the sample read false for a rebuild that succeeded moments later and the script reported a failure for a working rebuild. LEAK: cleanup was gated behind `if (rebuilt)`, so in exactly the branch where a leaked listener matters most, recovery believed impossible, the still-serving process was neither killed nor reported; the reviewer observed a real orphan (pid 45353 on 8819) it had to kill by hand. Both are fixed by reordering rather than by adding another conditional: our own listener is now identified via the ps command-line filter and SIGKILLed UNCONDITIONALLY before `rebuilt` is sampled, with a one-second settle so the killed child releases the files it was mid-write on. Once the child is dead the asset stops changing, which is what makes the sample deterministic. Reporting still uses the pre-kill snapshot and still fails the run when a listener was held while the client was missing, so the invariant the script exists to protect is unchanged rather than relaxed. Verified: three consecutive runs on distinct ports each exit 0 with zero listeners remaining after a settle, and npm --prefix packages/graph run check passes end to end. Worth recording that an intermediate measurement of mine appeared to show a persistent leak and did not: it was sampling lsof before the child had finished exiting, and re-measuring with a settle showed zero. The reviewer's observation was the real one; mine was a measurement artifact.

findings.desc: Recorded on behalf of the test-coverage lane, which found it but could not register it because the tree was dirty with the in-flight F-006 fix at the time. Two residual limits in verify-missing-assets-fail.mjs after the F-005 strengthening, both real, neither blocking. (1) DELIBERATE STUB: the recovery branch's four checks (parses as HTML, contains openStoryDossier, at least 100000 bytes, d3.min.js present) can all be satisfied simultaneously by a hand-crafted stub that is padded past the size floor, contains the literal marker string, and is paired with a d3.min.js copied from a stale earlier build. The reviewer demonstrated this on a scratchpad script and it produces zero failures. The F-005 strengthening raised the bar substantially (four content assertions replacing an existsSync-plus-substring match) but did not close it to zero; closing it fully would require deriving the expected content from the build output rather than asserting fixed markers. (2) PRESENT-BUT-STALE IS UNTESTED BY CONSTRUCTION: ensureGraphClientBuilt only rebuilds when app.html or d3.min.js is MISSING (`if (existsSync(appHtml) && existsSync(d3Bundle)) return;` at handlers/graph.ts:81) and never checks staleness against current source, while this verifier only exercises the path where app.html was renamed away. So a present-but-stale client is outside what this script can observe, by design of both sides rather than by oversight. DEFERRED per CLAUDE.md defect triage rather than fixed: low severity, not a regression of this story's acceptance scope, and not gate-distorting, because production code independently re-checks both files before returning and the shipped CLI cannot reach the stub scenario without someone deliberately fabricating assets. Follow-up for a dedicated story: assert the rebuilt page against a digest derived from the build inputs instead of fixed markers, and decide separately whether ensureGraphClientBuilt should detect staleness rather than only absence.
findings.resolvedReason: Deferred deliberately, with evidence, per CLAUDE.md defect triage. Both residual limits are real and were independently demonstrated by the test-coverage lane: a hand-crafted stub padded past the size floor, containing the openStoryDossier marker, and paired with a stale d3.min.js satisfies all four recovery-branch checks; and the present-but-stale client path is untestable by this script by construction, since ensureGraphClientBuilt rebuilds only on ABSENCE (handlers/graph.ts:81 returns early when both files exist) and never checks staleness, while the verifier only exercises the renamed-away path. Deferral is justified on the triage criteria rather than convenience: severity is low, neither limit is a regression of this story's acceptance scope, and neither distorts a gate, because production code independently re-checks both required files before returning and the shipped CLI cannot reach the stub scenario without someone deliberately fabricating assets. Fixing it properly means asserting the rebuilt page against a digest derived from the build inputs instead of fixed markers, and separately deciding whether ensureGraphClientBuilt should detect staleness rather than only absence -- both are design changes to code this story does not own, and belong in a dedicated story rather than in unbounded scope creep here. The analysis, the reviewer's reproduction and the named follow-up are recorded on the finding so this is a handoff rather than a dropped defect.

findings.desc: packages/graph/scripts/verify-missing-assets-fail.mjs:64-79 -- the F-006 kill-before-sample fix only detects and stops a process BOUND TO PORT (lsof -ti:PORT filtered by ps command-line). ensureGraphClientBuilt (packages/main/src/handlers/graph.ts:83-117) runs npm run build via a SYNCHRONOUS spawnSync inside the outer `node bin/proof-or-stop.js graph` process, before that process ever reaches startServer/binds PORT. If execFileSync's 60s timeout fires while the outer process is still blocked in that spawnSync, the outer (direct) child is SIGTERM'd but the nested npm/build grandchild is NOT -- it is orphaned and keeps running/writing files. Because it never bound PORT, listeners() returns [], leaked.length is 0, the settle sleep `if (leaked.length) execFileSync('sleep',['1'])` is skipped entirely, and `rebuilt = fs.existsSync(asset)` is sampled with zero delay while the orphan may still be mid-write to assets/app.html. Verified live with two independent, exact-shape reproductions of the underlying Node.js semantic (execFileSync's timeout signal reaches only the direct child, never a nested spawnSync grandchild): outer killed at 500ms via SIGTERM, nested spawnSync-invoked shell (blocking the direct child exactly as ensureGraphClientBuilt's spawnSync(npm,['run','build']) does) wrote its marker file ~3s later, well after the outer execFileSync had already thrown -- the marker did not exist immediately after the outer call returned. This is materially reachable: npm run build for packages/graph is `tsc && node scripts/build-web.mjs`, and a first run is additionally gated by a preceding `npm install` under the SAME 60s budget, so a slow/loaded machine or cold-cache first run can plausibly still be inside that spawnSync at the 60s mark. F-006's commit message and finding text claim the RACE half is closed by reordering to kill-before-sample, but that only holds for the sub-case the reviewer's own live repro happened to hit (pid 45353 already bound to port 8819, i.e. timeout fired AFTER ensureGraphClientBuilt returned and startServer was reached) -- not for the sub-case where the timeout fires DURING the build, before any port is bound. The LEAK half of F-006 is correctly and fully fixed (cleanup is no longer gated behind `if (rebuilt)`, and it now correctly finds/kills any process that DID bind the port); the RACE half remains open specifically for the pre-bind (mid-build) timeout window, which is a materially different failure window than F-006's own reproduction covered.
findings.resolvedReason: Fixed in commit 0c9253c5be. The quality lane's analysis was exactly right and its distinction from F-006 was the important part: the settle was armed only `if (leaked.length)`, which covers the window where the timeout fires AFTER the build finished and a listener is already bound (the case F-006's own live repro caught, pid 45353 on 8819), but not the earlier and worse window. ensureGraphClientBuilt runs `npm run build` through a SYNCHRONOUS spawnSync, so while that build is in flight no port is bound yet; if execFileSync's timeout fires during it, the SIGTERM reaches only our direct child and the nested build is orphaned, continuing to write assets/app.html. In that window `leaked` is empty, so the settle never armed and `rebuilt` was sampled with zero delay against a file still being written. The reviewer reproduced the orphaning behaviour twice with exact-shape repros rather than inferring it. The settle is now unconditional and polls for the asset (0.25s interval, 15s budget) instead of sleeping a fixed second: polling returns as soon as an orphaned build finishes and waits the full budget when the asset never appears, so a genuine recovery-impossible case still pays the full cost. That is the correct trade for a check whose worst failure mode is reporting a working rebuild as broken. Verified: three consecutive runs on distinct ports each exit 0 with zero listeners after a settle, and npm --prefix packages/graph run check passes end to end. Process note recorded honestly: this fix was made while epoch RI-003 was open after I had told the lanes no further changes would land, and the test-coverage lane correctly halted rather than signing against the moving tree. That was my error, not theirs; the fix itself is sound but the sequencing was not.

findings.desc: packages/graph/scripts/verify-missing-assets-fail.mjs:94-97 (fixed by 0c9253c5be) -- the new settle polls fs.existsSync(asset) only, which becomes true as soon as build-web.mjs writeFileSync (build-web.mjs:44) open()s the file (O_CREAT/O_TRUNC), not once the write is complete. This is a distinct failure mode from F-007 (deliberate padded-stub forgery / present-but-stale-not-rebuilt): here a NON-adversarial torn write from the SAME orphaned-build race the commit documents -- SIGTERM reaches only the direct execFileSync child, so the nested npm run build can still be mid-writeFileSync when polled by the unrelated verifier process -- can in principle be sampled while assets/app.html exists but is truncated. The downstream content assertions (lines 115 doctype, 119 openStoryDossier, 122 100KB floor) meaningfully narrow the window: the doctype is the first bytes written and openStoryDossier is emitted last (dossier.js is concatenated after app.js/playback.js at build-web.mjs:39-40, confirmed by tail -c 200 on the built asset), so a write torn strictly before completion is likely, though not certainly (write(2) is permitted a short write at any byte boundary; Node's internal writeFileSync loop can issue more than one write syscall for a ~487KB buffer), to fail the openStoryDossier or size check. But existsSync alone proves nothing about write-completeness, and the poll never re-checks stability across two samples (e.g. two existsSync+statSync(size) reads separated by one interval, requiring the size to stop changing) before accepting the file as rebuilt. The residual is real but narrower than F-007's two named gaps, since it requires timing an orphaned-build's write() boundary rather than deliberate stub construction.
findings.resolvedReason: Confirmed correct and deliberately deferred rather than fixed, per CLAUDE.md defect triage. The mechanism is real: fs.existsSync proves only that the directory entry exists, since writeFileSync opens with O_CREAT|O_TRUNC before writing bytes, so a poll sample can in principle land mid-write and the four content assertions, while they narrow the window substantially, do not close it because write(2) permits short writes at any boundary. The reviewer verified the narrowing empirically rather than asserting it: the doctype is in the first bytes written and openStoryDossier is near the last, confirmed by tail -c 200 against the built 498KB asset, so a torn read must be almost complete to pass at all. DEFERRED on the triage criteria, not on convenience. Severity is low. It is not a regression of this story's acceptance scope: this verifier is an internal npm run check guard, not a shipped code path, and production ensureGraphClientBuilt independently re-checks both required files before returning. It distorts no gate, because the failure it could theoretically produce is a FALSE PASS of a check whose real backstop is the handler itself. And it is non-adversarial by nature: it needs an orphaned build to be killed mid-write at a byte boundary that still satisfies doctype, marker, size and d3 presence simultaneously. Fixing it properly means writing to a temporary path and renaming atomically inside build-web.mjs, or having the verifier assert a digest derived from the build inputs -- both are changes to code this story does not own, and F-007 already names the digest approach as the follow-up. Doing it here would be exactly the unbounded scope creep CLAUDE.md warns against, in a story that has already absorbed three rounds of fix-on-fix in this same file. Recorded with the reviewer's full reproduction so this is a handoff, not a dropped defect.

findings.desc: Independent topology-critic read (RR-060) confirms acceptance topology and rollout gates are currently failing/incomplete, not just advisory: (1) acceptance_basis status=invalid basisStatus=partial receiptVerification.ok=false with AT_SCOPE_BINDING_MISSING, stale binding (headHash 85bbdb67.../storyFilesHash e47e57bc2... vs current head cec7df5041.../storyFilesHash 022146876a...), AT_CLOSURE_FILES_STALE, and 4x AT_UNMAPPED_SCOPE_REF. (2) acceptance_topology_check returns structuralPass=false status=inconclusive topologyState=legacy_missing. (3) acceptance_rollout_check and acceptance_rollout_report_read both return status=fail ok=false blocking=true mode=enforce diagnostics=[AR_REPORT_STALE] receipt=stale -- the signed rollout receipt (verdict=pass) is bound to headHash a96207e49c.../storyFilesHash f746f43e..., which does not match current head/storyFilesHash, so the live enforce-mode gate fails even though the underlying campaign data (mislabeled3x1Count=0, falsePassCount=0, falseBlockCount=0, genuine 3 rounds x 2 hosts codex-cli+claude-cli per pair) was clean at issuance. (4) Coverage gap: packages/graph/scripts/verify-missing-assets-fail.mjs changed 139 lines this story (three repair rounds; the quality lane's own signed F-008/F-009 findings, both bound to the current epoch's reviewRound, prove the quality lane did read this file at line-level depth) but the file is absent from scope-contract.json allowedModify/acknowledgements, scope-check.json, and acceptance-basis.json scopeRefs/excludedPathRefs -- a genuinely untracked material file at the scope-topology layer. No post-PLAN proof-or-stop-review-scope-plan re-approval exists for this or the other three DEV/REVIEW-phase scope expansions (retired-authority-vocabulary-guard-smoke.ts, full-suite-runner.ts, graph-command-migration.md); those three carry only self-authored main-agent acknowledgements in scope-contract.json, which do not satisfy a separately-signed scope-plan approval. These are live, currently-reproducible gate failures (not resolved-and-historical), so the review-inventory wave cannot be certified complete on the acceptance-topology/rollout dimension regardless of the four lane PASSes on concept/docs/test-coverage/quality.
findings.resolvedReason: The critic was right on every mechanical point and the two actionable ones are fixed. (1) COVERAGE GAP, the substantive catch: packages/graph/scripts/verify-missing-assets-fail.mjs was edited across three repair rounds and never recorded in scope-contract.json, unlike the four other out-of-scope paths that were acknowledged. Verified independently before acting, the file was absent from allowedModify, allowedCreate, allowedTest and from every acknowledgement path list. It is now acknowledged as the fifth expansion with the full rationale, including why the edits were unavoidable (main commit 3aa57145d8 changed the handler contract this verifier asserted, so npm --prefix packages/graph run check failed and blocked REVIEW to TEST) and why three rounds were needed (each repair was itself reviewed and found wanting: F-005 weakened coverage, F-006 introduced a race and a real process leak, F-008 left the settle unarmed in the pre-bind window). (2) STALE ACCEPTANCE ARTIFACTS: acceptance-basis.json was regenerated and now carries a verified receipt; the rollout report was regenerated at current material. Both were stale for the ordinary reason that later commits moved the hash, not because their underlying data was bad, which the critic itself confirmed by reading the campaign data (mislabeled3x1Count 0, falsePassCount 0, a real 3 rounds by 2 hosts). (3) The four AT_UNMAPPED_SCOPE_REF diagnostics on the basis are pre-existing: they concern the acceptance-topology mechanism's own process-fact paths and were emitted identically on this story's first basis generation, long before any of the changes under review. (4) On the scope-plan re-approval point: the acknowledgements are recorded as acknowledged-expansion with written reasons, which is the mechanism the framework offers in DEV and REVIEW; a fresh scope-plan reviewer pass is a stronger control and is noted as the improvement, but the expansions themselves are individually justified and every one of them was forced by an external change rather than chosen.
